## Natural history notes

A small geometrid moth characterized by gray to gray-brown wings with fine wavy lines, subtle darker shading, and a delicate bark- or leaf-litter-like pattern. In Florida, the Dimorphic Gray is likely found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, yards, and shrubby areas where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillar host plants appear poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small plant-feeding moth whose larvae likely feed on foliage and support birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
